source_title: News Five Bengaluru Friends Killed As Helicopter Crashes Near Badrinath In Uttarakhand
source_excerpt: “Gone too soon, brother,” Bengaluru Police Inspector Arun Salunke had written on Instagram on August 28, mourning the death of a colleague from the Central Crime Branch (CCB). A little over a month later, the 44-year-old was himself killed when the helicopter carrying him and four friends back from Badrinath crashed near Jyotirmath (Joshimath) in Uttarakhand's Chamoli district on Friday. The five friends had embarked on the Char Dham pilgrimage three days earlier and were expected to return to Bengaluru on Friday evening. Their families and friends were waiting for them when news of the crash broke. One of the passengers had spoken to a childhood friend just hours before the accident, saying that the group was waiting inside the helicopter for the weather to improve. Bengaluru CCB Inspector Among Those Killed Salunke, a 2007-batch Karnataka Police officer, hailed from Aratal village in Athani taluk of Belagavi district. He completed his education at Bengaluru's MS Ramaiah Institute of Technology before joining the police force. During his career, he served at Halasuru police station and in the Criminal Investigation Department before being posted as an inspector with the Bengaluru Police's Central Crime Branch. Dasappa, who owns the apartment building where Salunke had lived as a tenant for three years, remembered him as a friendly person who shared a cordial relationship with the residents. “Arun Salunke was a very good person. He was friendly with everyone in the apartment,” Dasappa was cited by an HT report. Another resident, Gajendra, who had known the inspector for three years, recalled meeting him during morning walks. According to him, Salunke would usually leave for duty at around 10 am and return at approximately 10 pm. Dasappa also said that Shankar Gowda, an advocate who was among those on the pilgrimage, occasionally visited the apartment. Who Were The Five Passengers Killed In The Crash? The other passengers killed in the helicopter crash were identified as H S Nataraj, 51, Prathap Ningraju, 41, Sudheer K, 49, and Shankar Gowda, 39. Uttarakhand authorities said all five passengers were residents of Bengaluru. Nataraj, a native of Huliyurdurga in Tumakuru district, headed the Vidya Bharati educational institution. Gowda was an advocate, while Prathap, who hailed from Bachanahalli in Sakaleshapura taluk of Hassan district, worked as a civil contractor. ALSO READ: INDIA Bloc Holds ‘Public Impeachment’ Of CEC Gyanesh Kumar, Lists Six Charges Against Him Prathap had moved to Bengaluru around 15 years ago and lived in Thanisandra with his wife and two sons, who study in Classes 7 and 3. His family had been expecting him to return home on Friday evening. Prajwal, a coffee planter and Prathap's brother-in-law, said the five friends had left for the pilgrimage three days earlier. “We were all waiting for them to come back, but instead received the tragic news,” he said. “He was happily married and had a family life. The entire family is in tears,” Prajwal added. Nataraj Spoke To Childhood Friend Hours Before Crash For Nagesh, a businessman from Huliyurdurga and Nataraj's childhood friend, the tragedy was particularly difficult because of their last conversation. Nagesh said Nataraj called him at around 11 am on Friday from inside the helicopter. The group was waiting for the weather to clear before taking off. “He told me that he was sitting inside the helicopter and waiting for the weather to clear. The pilot had reportedly told them that the area was covered in thick fog and that they would have to wait until visibility improved. When I asked him about the weather, he said it was extremely cold there,” Nagesh recalled. Karnataka Leaders Express Condolences Karnataka Chief Minister D K Shivakumar expressed grief over the deaths and said the state government was coordinating with Uttarakhand officials to bring the bodies back to Karnataka as soon as possible. “The news that a helicopter en route from Badrinath to Dehradun crashed near Joshimath in Uttarakhand's Chamoli district, killing the pilot from Delhi and five passengers from Karnataka, has caused profound shock and grief,” he said in a statement. “Discussions are underway with Uttarakhand officials to bring the bodies back to Karnataka as soon as possible, and the state government stands in solidarity with the families of the deceased during this time of grief,” Shivakumar added. Karnataka Minister Priyank Kharge also offered condolences, describing the loss of Kannadigas in the crash as heartbreaking. He said Salunke's death was particularly painful for the police department and extended his sympathies to the families of all five passengers and the pilot. “The fact that Arun Salunke, a CCB inspector who had gone on a trip, has lost his life in this tragedy is an extremely painful matter for the Police Department,” Kharge said, praying for peace for those killed and strength for their bereaved families. उत्तराखंड के चमोली जिले में बदरीनाथ के पास एक हेलिकॉप्टर दुर्घटना में बेंगलुरु के पांच दोस्तों की मौत हो गई। यह दुर्घटना शुक्रवार को ज्योतिर्मठ (जोशीमठ) के पास हुई, जब सभी पांचों लोग अपनी चार धाम यात्रा पूरी करने के बाद लौट रहे थे।

## मृतकों की पहचान और पृष्ठभूमि
रिपोर्ट्स के अनुसार, मृतकों में बेंगलुरु पुलिस की सेंट्रल क्राइम ब्रांच (CCB) के इंस्पेक्टर अरुण सालुंके भी शामिल थे। 44 वर्षीय सालुंके 2007 बैच के कर्नाटक पुलिस अधिकारी थे। इस हादसे में जान गंवाने वाले अन्य चार यात्रियों की पहचान एच.एस. नटराज (51), प्रताप निंगराजू (41), सुधीर के. (49) और शंकर गौड़ा (39) के रूप में हुई है। उत्तराखंड प्राधिकारियों ने पुष्टि की है कि ये सभी पांचों यात्री बेंगलुरु के निवासी थे।

* **अरुण सालुंके:** बेंगलुरु सीसीबी में इंस्पेक्टर, जो मूल रूप से बेलगावी जिले के अथानी तालुक के अराताल गांव के रहने वाले थे।
* **एच.एस. नटराज:** विद्या भारती शैक्षणिक संस्थान के प्रमुख, तुमकुरु जिले के हुलियुरदुरगा के मूल निवासी।
* **प्रताप निंगराजू:** एक सिविल ठेकेदार, जो हसन जिले के सक्लेशपुरा तालुक के बचानहल्ली के रहने वाले थे।
* **शंकर गौड़ा:** एक वकील, जो इस तीर्थयात्रा पर गए थे।
* **सुधीर के.:** इस दुखद दुर्घटना में जान गंवाने वाले पांचवें यात्री।

## दुर्घटना से जुड़ी मुख्य बातें

* **खराब मौसम:** एक यात्री ने दुर्घटना से कुछ घंटे पहले अपने एक बचपन के दोस्त को फोन करके बताया था कि उनका समूह हेलिकॉप्टर के अंदर बैठा है और मौसम साफ होने का इंतजार कर रहा है।
* **वापसी की उम्मीद:** ये पांचों दोस्त तीन दिन पहले चार धाम यात्रा पर निकले थे और शुक्रवार शाम को बेंगलुरु लौटने वाले थे।
* **नेताओं की प्रतिक्रिया:** कर्नाटक के उपमुख्यमंत्री डी.के. शिवकुमार और मंत्री प्रियांक खर्गे ने इस हादसे पर गहरा शोक व्यक्त किया है।

## आधिकारिक समन्वय और आगे की प्रक्रिया
कर्नाटक सरकार ने कहा है कि वह उत्तराखंड के अधिकारियों के संपर्क में है ताकि मृतकों के पार्थिव शरीर को जल्द से जल्द कर्नाटक वापस लाया जा सके। इस दुर्घटना के कारणों और आधिकारिक जांच के ब्योरे की पुष्टि संबंधित विमानन और आपदा प्रबंधन अधिकारियों द्वारा की जानी अभी बाकी है।

en_body:
## Tragedy Strikes During Char Dham Pilgrimage

Five friends from Bengaluru, including a Central Crime Branch (CCB) police inspector, were killed when the helicopter they were traveling in crashed near Jyotirmath (Joshimath) in Uttarakhand's Chamoli district on Friday. According to reports, the group had embarked on the Char Dham pilgrimage three days prior to the accident and were scheduled to return to Bengaluru.

State authorities confirmed that all five deceased passengers were residents of Bengaluru. The victims have been identified as:

* **Arun Salunke**, 44, a 2007-batch Karnataka Police officer serving as an inspector with the Bengaluru CCB.
* **H S Nataraj**, 51, head of the Vidya Bharati educational institution.
* **Shankar Gowda**, 39, an advocate.
* **Prathap Ningraju**, 41, a civil contractor.
* **Sudheer K**, 49.

Reports indicate that the pilot, hailing from Delhi, also lost his life in the crash.

## Final Communications and Weather Conditions

According to accounts from family members and acquaintances, one of the passengers, H S Nataraj, spoke with a childhood friend via phone at approximately 11 am on Friday. During the conversation from inside the aircraft, Nataraj reportedly stated that the group was waiting for thick fog to clear and visibility to improve before taking off.

## Official Responses and Next Steps

Karnataka Chief Minister D K Shivakumar expressed condolences and stated that the state government is actively coordinating with officials in Uttarakhand to facilitate the return of the victims' bodies to Karnataka. Minister Priyank Kharge also offered public expressions of grief, acknowledging the impact of the loss on the police department and the families involved.

* **Verification**: Official details regarding the accident's cause are subject to ongoing investigations by aviation and regional authorities in Uttarakhand.
* **Practical Implications**: Families and associates affected by the incident are advised to monitor official updates from state coordination desks regarding repatriation procedures.
